content: A pendant group, also referred to as a side group, is a molecular group that is covalently bonded to the backbone chain of a larger molecule. Typically, this larger molecule is a polymer. For instance, in the case of polystyrene, the phenyl groups serve as the pendant groups attached to the polymer chain. Pendant groups that are large and bulky, such as adamantyl groups, tend to increase the glass transition temperature (Tg) of the polymer. This occurs because their size and structure hinder the polymer chains from sliding past one another with ease. Conversely, shorter alkyl pendant groups can decrease the glass transition temperature. This reduction in Tg is attributed to a lubricant-like effect, which facilitates the movement of the polymer chains.
